title: The doctors' band Swing Four Seven and the Louis Armstrong imitator Theis Nyegaard
summary: A band of Danish doctors with a dentist arranger swings like 52nd Street and gave him a televised farewell party; another leader plays only Armstrong's repertoire.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Then there's a wonderful band there that I've made lots of tapes with and I recorded lots

of tapes with them; and, I did a couple of television shows. They call themselves "Swing Four Seven" and they've got the most fantastic rhythm section I ever heard. They have a dentist - my dentist by the way - who plays tenor saxophone, clarinet and alto and writes for this band and I want to tell you - you'd swear you're on 52nd Street. They've got that marvelous swing - that old swing era thing that they were doing in those days and he does a job on it. And, then, there's another band there that's very surprising; two guys have it; they call the band Theis-Nyegaard "Ty So Nugard" now, those are two different guys. Tyce is a guy that - you can't believe this until you hear him; he can't play anything but what Louie Armstrong has already played.
My God, you mean he just patterns everything he does---

---he sings like Louie; he plays like Louie and what's strange about it is that if you work with that band, and if you play anything else but a Louie number - that Louie has done in his lifetime, he is lost.
Well, does that mean that they're just simply memorized---

Well - not only memorized but he only plays things that Louie Armstrong played; of course, he has a hell of a repertoire because Louie made a lot of things, you know, and he sings like him and then I did a lot

All doctors and these-- and for my birthday, they gave me a stethoscope with a trumpet on the other end of it -- you know -- a little something. Anyway, they threw my farewell party, which was televised. Now, these guys would surprise you today.
Yeah - here's a bunch of guys - some of them are pretty old - some of them are 68 -- near 70---

Yeah - they're almost my age. The point is here they sit there and play absolutely fantastically well and they're really working doctors and you know doctors are busy as hell in Denmark. But, they find time to do this and they've provided me with a lot of work because they add me to the band, you know. And, of course, I can play all the things that they play--
And they have a trumpet player and you know, I'm the great second trumpet player in the world--
So, you just play second to him and then take your own solo--
